note: Original classroom practice with fictional scenarios. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.topic: Apprenticeship and Career Opportunities in Creative and Design Arts
questions.learningObjective: Identify features of apprenticeship in a creative workplace.
questions.prompt: Four pupils describe what happens at a fictional community theatre. Which description provides the clearest evidence that an apprenticeship is taking place?
questions.answer: A trainee practises making props in stages and revises them after feedback from an experienced prop maker.
questions.explanation: Guided practice and feedback across successive tasks show that the trainee is learning a craft through work.
options: A visitor watches the opening scene and takes a programme home.
A volunteer hands out tickets before a single show.
A trainee practises making props in stages and revises them after feedback from an experienced prop maker.
A customer orders a painted backdrop and collects it later.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.topic: Apprenticeship and Career Opportunities in Creative and Design Arts
questions.learningObjective: Explain how repeated supervised practice builds a creative skill.
questions.prompt: At a textile studio, an apprentice prints a border whose corners fail to join. The mentor points out where the repeat begins and asks the apprentice to make a second trial on scrap fabric. Explain how the feedback and trial can improve the finished border.
questions.answer: The feedback helps the apprentice locate the break in the repeat. On scrap fabric the apprentice can test a different starting position. Comparing the trial corners shows whether the border joins before using the final fabric.
questions.explanation: The mentor makes the error specific, and the trial gives the apprentice a way to check a correction before committing materials.

markingGuide.description: Locates the problem in the meeting of the repeated motif.
Explains that the trial lets the apprentice change and test the starting position.
States that the trial result can be checked before printing the final fabric.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.topic: Apprenticeship and Career Opportunities in Creative and Design Arts
questions.learningObjective: Match a stated creative learning goal to the work taught by a mentor.
questions.prompt: A fictional arts centre lists four supervised learning sessions. Ngozi wants to learn how recorded dialogue and background sounds are combined for a short film. Which session best matches her goal?
questions.answer: Working with a sound editor to adjust speech and background tracks against a scene.
questions.explanation: The sound editor’s session lets her practise combining the kinds of audio named in the learning goal.
options: Working with a costume maker to fit and label garments.
Working with a sound editor to adjust speech and background tracks against a scene.
Working with a camera assistant to record shots from different angles.
Working with a storyboard artist to sketch a scene in panels.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.topic: Apprenticeship and Career Opportunities in Creative and Design Arts
questions.learningObjective: Use evidence about tasks and supervision to compare possible learning opportunities.
questions.prompt: Two fictional design studios describe their training. Studio A lets learners draft sample signs, discuss readability with a designer and revise one design. Studio B asks learners to pack completed signs and record quantities. Which plan better suits a learner who wants to design signs? Give two pieces of evidence and one question to ask about progress before choosing.
questions.answer: Choose Studio A. Learners draft signs and receive a designer’s feedback on readability. Ask what criteria the designer uses to decide when a learner is ready to work on a more complex sign.
questions.explanation: The choice follows the stated learning goal. Asking how progress is judged helps the learner understand how the training develops over time.

markingGuide.description: Identifies drafting sample signs as relevant practice.
Identifies feedback or revision as a relevant feature.
Asks a question about feedback, progression or how learning is assessed.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.topic: Apprenticeship and Career Opportunities in Creative and Design Arts
questions.learningObjective: Identify creative occupations associated with a community production.
questions.prompt: A youth theatre needs an illustrated event flyer and a performer to compose a short original tune for the opening. Name a suitable creative occupation for each task and describe what each person would deliver.
questions.answer: A graphic designer could deliver a flyer layout with an illustration and readable event details. A musician or composer could deliver a short original opening tune.
questions.explanation: The flyer communicates in visual form. The tune provides musical material for the performance.

markingGuide.description: Names graphic designer, graphic artist or another defensible visual-design role.
Describes a flyer with a visual layout and event information.
Describes a short original tune for the opening.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Recognise evidence of professional artistic practice from a work description.
questions.prompt: A display label describes Zainab taking a commission for a mural. She discusses the theme with the client, agrees a delivery date, prepares a sketch and completes the mural. Which detail most clearly shows her work as a professional artist in this case?
questions.answer: She undertakes a commission and delivers artwork to an agreed brief.
questions.explanation: The commission and agreed brief show that she is applying artistic skills to a professional responsibility.
options: She uses the same colours as the school uniform.
She keeps a sketchbook at home.
She admires the work of another painter.
She undertakes a commission and delivers artwork to an agreed brief.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Identify a professional art role from characteristic materials and work.
questions.prompt: A craft cooperative needs a maker who can shape clay vessels and have them fired for an exhibition of ceramic work. Which professional’s usual practice best matches the brief?
questions.explanation: Ceramists work with clay and other ceramic materials. Firing is a characteristic process in producing ceramic objects.
options: Ceramist.
Graphic designer.
Textile designer.
Dramatist.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Explain how two art professionals communicate using different features of their work.
questions.prompt: For a library entrance, one artist makes a freestanding sculpture of a reader, while another designs a wall sign pointing towards the reading room. Describe a feature each artist can use to help the work serve its purpose.
questions.answer: The sculptor can shape the reader and book so they are recognisable from several approaches. The graphic designer can use a clear arrow and large lettering that visitors can read while walking.
questions.explanation: Three-dimensional form can communicate an idea from different viewpoints. Legible lettering and directional symbols guide movement.

markingGuide.description: Names a relevant feature of the sculpture such as recognisable form or pose.
Connects that feature to communicating the reading theme from an intended viewpoint.
Names a feature of the sign such as an arrow or legible lettering.
Connects that feature to helping visitors find the room.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish textile design from fashion design using examples of work.
questions.prompt: A makers’ fair displays two development boards. Board P shows a repeated motif tested across the width of a cloth. Board Q shows sleeve shapes tested on a garment to improve movement. Assign the most relevant design specialism to each board and justify both choices.
questions.answer: P fits textile design because it develops how the motif repeats on the cloth. Q fits fashion design because it develops the shape and fit of a garment for the wearer.
questions.explanation: The roles can overlap. The main design problem shown on each board indicates the relevant specialism.

markingGuide.description: Links P to designing a repeat on fabric.
Links Q to garment shape, fit or movement.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Recognise a characteristic feature of a choreographer’s work.
questions.prompt: A school arts team has already selected its music. Which contribution best demonstrates the work of the choreographer preparing the group dance?
questions.answer: Arranging the dancers’ movements and entries to fit the planned sequence.
questions.explanation: Choreography organises movement over time and space. Entries help structure when performers join a sequence.
options: Balancing the volume of the recorded music and announcements.
Arranging the dancers’ movements and entries to fit the planned sequence.
Painting a backdrop that suggests the location of the story.
Editing a recording to join shots from two cameras.
